name: Glint Shard
geological_features: Fractured regolith plains with exposed metallic veins
Impact crater chains suggesting ancient collision cascades
Subsurface cavern networks formed by volatile outgassing
specific_features: The Vault — a naturally shielded cavern system three kilometers beneath the surface, accessible only through a narrow fissure masked by radar-reflective mineral deposits
Anomalous thermal signatures in the deep caverns inconsistent with natural geological processes
Surface albedo irregularities suggesting recent artificial resurfacing of select crater floors
description: Glint Shard is barely a world at all — a jagged, potato-shaped rock less than eight hundred kilometers across, tumbling through the outer reaches of a sparsely charted system. Its surface is a monotony of grey regolith and fractured stone, pocked with overlapping impact craters that speak to billions of years of unshielded bombardment. With negligible gravity and no atmosphere, it registers on most surveys as unremarkable debris.

That anonymity is precisely its value. The thermal signature is wrong — deep-scan sensors detect warmth in the subsurface caverns that no natural process can explain, and certain crater floors show spectral profiles consistent with recent regolith redistribution. Someone has been here, and recently, and they have gone to considerable effort to make it look like no one has.

Smuggler caches in asteroid bodies are common enough, but Glint Shard's Vault is something more ambitious. Intercepted freight manifests and cross-referenced shipping anomalies suggest a waystation capable of servicing mid-size freighters, with enough stored supplies and fuel to support extended operations far from any patrolled lane. The fissure entrance is virtually invisible to orbital scans, masked by naturally occurring radar-reflective minerals that someone has very cleverly left undisturbed.

The question is not whether Glint Shard harbors a smuggling operation — the evidence is damning enough. The question is whose operation it is and what they are moving through it. The rock sits at a navigational crossroads between three contested systems, making it ideal for running embargoed technology, unregistered biologics, or worse. Any approach must assume the Vault is monitored, trapped, or both.
